---
name: webui/use-autogenerated-mojo-browser-proxy
description: >-
  Check when WebUI TypeScript code defines a custom BrowserProxy class for Mojo
  interfaces, calls .getRemote() directly, or manually binds Mojo pipes.
rubric: design
severity: should_fix
---

**Rule.** Always access WebUI Mojo interfaces through the autogenerated
`browserProxyFactory` (and `BrowserProxy` type) exported by `*.mojom-webui.js`
whenever the `.mojom` file qualifies for an autogenerated proxy. A `.mojom` file
automatically generates `BrowserProxy` and `browserProxyFactory` when it defines
a factory interface (whose name ends with `Factory` or contains
`PageHandlerFactory`) with a method that accepts either:

- 2 parameters: a `pending_remote` and a `pending_receiver` (in either parameter
  order), or
- 1 parameter: a `pending_receiver` (for handlers without a callback router).

If a WebUI `.mojom` file does not yet qualify—especially when the `.mojom`
interface is being added or modified in the same CL—check whether it can be
trivially made conformant so `browserProxyFactory` is generated instead of
writing a bespoke `BrowserProxy` (for example, naming the bootstrap interface
with a `Factory` suffix such as `PageHandlerFactory`, adding a
`PageHandlerFactory` rather than binding a WebUI `PageHandler` directly via
`PageHandler.getRemote()`, or keeping the factory method parameters to just the
`pending_remote` and/or `pending_receiver`). Do not ask authors to refactor
pre-existing shared/system service `.mojom` interfaces or multi-handler
factories that are outside the scope of the CL.

For the factory's primary handler and callback router, do not write bespoke
`BrowserProxy` / `BrowserProxyImpl` classes to hold `handler` and
`callbackRouter`, and do not manually instantiate `*Remote` / `*CallbackRouter`
or call `*Factory.getRemote()` with `bindNewPipeAndPassReceiver()` /
`bindNewPipeAndPassRemote()` (secondary Mojo pipes dynamically bound via methods
on an already-created handler may still be instantiated and bound manually).

Use `browserProxyFactory.getInstance()` in production code. In tests, use
`browserProxyFactory.createForTest(handler)` followed by
`browserProxyFactory.setInstance(instance)` for 2-way interfaces (with a
callback router), or call `browserProxyFactory.setInstance({handler})` directly
for 1-way handler-only interfaces (which use `MojoHandlerProxyFactory` and do
not have `createForTest()`). If a WebUI also needs non-Mojo browser proxy
methods (e.g., `chrome.send` or `sendWithPromise` calls), place those in a
separate browser proxy rather than wrapping the Mojo interfaces in a custom
class.

**Why.** Hand-written Mojo `BrowserProxy` classes duplicate boilerplate
singleton management, pipe binding, and test setup that
`MojoBrowserProxyFactory` and `MojoHandlerProxyFactory` in
`//resources/mojo/mojo_browser_proxy.js` already provide with full type safety.
See `docs/webui/webui_explainer.md#mojo`.

## Examples

Bad:

```ts
// my_feature_browser_proxy.ts — unnecessary bespoke Mojo proxy boilerplate
import type {PageHandlerInterface} from './my_feature.mojom-webui.js';
import {PageCallbackRouter, PageHandlerFactory, PageHandlerRemote} from './my_feature.mojom-webui.js';

export interface MyFeatureBrowserProxy {
  handler: PageHandlerInterface;
  callbackRouter: PageCallbackRouter;
}

export class MyFeatureBrowserProxyImpl implements MyFeatureBrowserProxy {
  handler: PageHandlerInterface;
  callbackRouter: PageCallbackRouter;

  private constructor() {
    this.handler = new PageHandlerRemote();
    this.callbackRouter = new PageCallbackRouter();
    PageHandlerFactory.getRemote().createPageHandler(
        this.callbackRouter.$.bindNewPipeAndPassRemote(),
        this.handler.$.bindNewPipeAndPassReceiver());
  }

  static getInstance(): MyFeatureBrowserProxy {
    return instance || (instance = new MyFeatureBrowserProxyImpl());
  }

  static setInstance(obj: MyFeatureBrowserProxy) {
    instance = obj;
  }
}

let instance: MyFeatureBrowserProxy|null = null;
```

Good:

```ts
// app.ts — access the Mojo interfaces directly via the autogenerated
// browserProxyFactory (any non-Mojo methods belong in a separate proxy)
import {browserProxyFactory} from './my_feature.mojom-webui.js';
import type {BrowserProxy} from './my_feature.mojom-webui.js';

export class MyFeatureAppElement extends CrLitElement {
  private proxy_: BrowserProxy = browserProxyFactory.getInstance();

  override connectedCallback() {
    super.connectedCallback();
    this.proxy_.handler.doSomething();
  }
}

// app_test.ts — use createForTest() + setInstance() for 2-way interfaces (or
// browserProxyFactory.setInstance({handler}) directly for 1-way handler-only
// interfaces)
import {browserProxyFactory, PageHandlerRemote} from 'chrome://my-feature/my_feature.mojom-webui.js';
import type {PageRemote} from 'chrome://my-feature/my_feature.mojom-webui.js';
import {TestMock} from 'chrome://webui-test/test_mock.js';

suite('MyFeatureAppTest', () => {
  let handler: TestMock<PageHandlerRemote>&PageHandlerRemote;
  let pageRemote: PageRemote;

  setup(() => {
    document.body.innerHTML = window.trustedTypes!.emptyHTML;
    handler = TestMock.fromClass(PageHandlerRemote);
    const {instance, remote} = browserProxyFactory.createForTest(handler);
    browserProxyFactory.setInstance(instance);
    pageRemote = remote;
  });
});
```
